boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Agnes Scott College
boards.description: Late-night dining options for Agnes Scott students range from on-campus grill favorites to the 24-hour staples of downtown Decatur.

cards.title: Mollie's Grill
cards.subtitle: Alston Campus Center
cards.notes: Visit the lower level of Alston for grilled sandwiches and snacks. It is the primary on-campus spot for late-night bites using student meal plan declining balance dollars.
cards.short_summary: The central on-campus late-night dining hub at Agnes Scott College.
cards.evidence_claim: Mollie's Grill is located in the lower level of the Alston Campus Center and serves grilled favorites and convenience items.
cards.access_notes: Open during academic semesters; check current campus dining schedules for specific late-night closing times.

cards.title: Waffle House on McDonough
cards.subtitle: 515 N McDonough St
cards.notes: Walk to this 24-hour staple just north of campus for classic breakfast fare. It is a frequent destination for students seeking a booth and hashbrowns at any hour.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour breakfast institution located within walking distance of the college.
cards.evidence_claim: The Waffle House at 515 N. McDonough Street in Decatur is open 24 hours a day.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams
cards.subtitle: Decatur Square
cards.notes: Head to the square for artisan scoops until midnight on weekends. It is a popular spot for a post-study dessert run in the heart of downtown Decatur.
cards.short_summary: A popular ice cream shop on Decatur Square with late weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Jeni's Decatur Square is open until 11:00 PM Sunday-Thursday and until Midnight Friday-Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Cook Out
cards.subtitle: Lawrenceville Hwy
cards.notes: Drive to this regional favorite for late-night trays and milkshakes. Known for staying open until 3:00 AM or later, it serves as a primary late-night drive-thru option.
cards.short_summary: A classic Southern late-night drive-thru known for its variety of milkshakes.
cards.evidence_claim: Cook Out locations typically stay open until 3:30 AM or 4:30 AM, especially near college campuses.
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:30 AM Sunday-Thursday and 4:30 AM Friday-Saturday.

cards.title: Besto (formerly Victory)
cards.subtitle: 340 Church St
cards.notes: Visit this rebranded American-Italian spot for sandwiches and late-night service. It maintains the casual, student-friendly atmosphere of its predecessor in downtown Decatur.
cards.short_summary: A casual American-Italian restaurant in downtown Decatur offering late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: Victory Sandwich Bar rebranded to Besto in July 2026, continuing to offer casual dining at 340 Church St.
cards.source_title: Victory Sandwich Bar rebranding to Besto in Decatur
cards.access_notes: Check current hours for late-night service; historically open until midnight or later.

cards.title: The Iberian Pig
cards.subtitle: 121 Sycamore St
cards.notes: Enjoy Spanish tapas on the square until 11:00 PM on weekends. It offers a more upscale late-evening dining experience for students and visitors in Decatur.
cards.short_summary: A Spanish tapas restaurant on Decatur Square with late weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Iberian Pig in Decatur is open until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Butter & Cream
cards.subtitle: 416 Church St
cards.notes: Stop by for small-batch ice cream until 11:00 PM daily. This local favorite is known for its handcrafted flavors and proximity to the Decatur Square.
cards.short_summary: A local handcrafted ice cream shop with consistent late-evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Butter & Cream in Decatur is open until 11:00 PM every day.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM daily.

cards.title: Raging Burrito & Taco
cards.subtitle: 141 Sycamore St
cards.notes: Grab a burrito on the patio until 10:00 PM on Fridays. A long-standing Decatur favorite, it provides a casual atmosphere for late-evening meals near the square.
cards.short_summary: A casual Mexican restaurant on Decatur Square with late-evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Raging Burrito is open until 10:00 PM on Fridays.
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM on Fridays; other nights close at 9:00 PM or 9:30 PM.

cards.title: Black Cat Coffee
cards.subtitle: Alston Campus Center
cards.notes: Get your caffeine fix on campus at this student-run cafe. It serves Starbucks coffee and light snacks, often staying open late during peak study periods.
cards.short_summary: The primary on-campus coffee shop at Agnes Scott College.
cards.evidence_claim: Black Cat Coffee is located adjacent to Mollie's Grill in the Alston Campus Center and serves coffee and snacks.
cards.access_notes: Check current campus dining schedules for specific late-night closing times.

cards.title: Chick-fil-A Downtown Decatur
cards.subtitle: 101 W Ponce de Leon Ave
cards.notes: Visit this downtown location for a quick meal until 10:00 PM. It is a reliable option for students looking for familiar fast food within walking distance of campus.
cards.short_summary: A centrally located fast-food option in downtown Decatur.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chick-fil-A in Downtown Decatur is open until 10:00 PM Monday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM Monday-Saturday; closed on Sundays.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the specific study nooks, quiet terraces, and student-centered lounges that define daily life at Agnes Scott College beyond the standard tour route.

cards.title: The Fireplace Nook
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Cozy up by the grand fireplace in the Main Reading Room. It is a favorite spot for students to curl up with a blanket during winter study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A cozy study area featuring a grand fireplace and comfortable seating in the library's main hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Reading Room on Floor 1 of McCain Library features couches by a fireplace where students are known to study and even use blankets.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; accessible to all students with a valid ID.

cards.title: The Rocking Chair Terrace
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Head to this outdoor terrace to find rocking chairs and reliable WiFi. It is a designated spot where students can take cell phone calls or study in the fresh air.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor library terrace equipped with rocking chairs and WiFi for fresh-air studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Elizabeth Henderson Cameron Reading Terrace features rocking chairs and WiFi, and is noted as a place to take cell phone calls.
cards.source_title: Favorite Study Spots in McCain Library
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space accessible through the library during operating hours.

cards.title: The Scenic Half-Moon Couch
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Ground Floor
cards.notes: Look for the half-moon couch in this room for a scenic view of the Science Quad. It offers a quieter alternative to the main floors for focused work.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor reading room with a signature half-moon couch and views of the Science Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The Elmore Reading Room on the ground floor features scenic seating facing the Science Quad and a half-moon couch.
cards.access_notes: Located on the ground floor of McCain Library; accessible via stairs or elevator.

cards.title: The Fireplace Lounge
cards.subtitle: Alston Campus Center
cards.notes: Affectionately called the 'Fireplace Lounge,' this spot in the Alston Campus Center is perfect for quiet reading or small student gatherings with campus views.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable campus center lounge known for its grand fireplace and picturesque views.
cards.evidence_claim: The Amelia Davis Luchsinger Lounge is affectionately dubbed the 'Fireplace Lounge' and features comfortable furniture and campus views.
cards.source_title: Small Group Venues | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Located within the Wallace McPherson Alston Campus Center; open to students daily.

cards.title: The Hidden Alcove
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Floor 3
cards.notes: Seek out the hidden alcove on the third floor for what students call the 'best seats in the house.' It is a prime spot for silent, uninterrupted study.
cards.short_summary: A secluded third-floor alcove designated for silent study and highly prized by students.
cards.evidence_claim: McCain Library's third floor contains a 'Hidden Alcove' described as having the 'best seats in the house' for silent study.
cards.access_notes: Floor 3 is a designated silent study floor; please maintain quiet in this area.

cards.title: The Commuter Hub
cards.subtitle: Alston Campus Center
cards.notes: A dedicated space for commuter students to relax between classes. It features lockers and comfortable seating to make campus life easier for those living off-site.
cards.short_summary: A specialized lounge in the campus center providing lockers and relaxation space for commuters.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alston Campus Center provides lounges specifically for commuter students along with lockers for their use.
cards.source_title: Commuter Student Information | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Primarily for commuter students; lockers can be checked out at the Hudson Center.

cards.title: The Science Atrium
cards.subtitle: Bullock Science Center
cards.notes: This bright, multi-story atrium is a central meeting point in the Bullock Science Center. It is a popular spot for students to gather before labs or for group projects.
cards.short_summary: A spacious, light-filled atrium serving as the social and collaborative heart of the science building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mary Brown Bullock Science Center features the Baker Atrium as a highlighted facility for gatherings.
cards.source_title: Small Group Venues | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; accessible to all students.

cards.title: The Campbell Atrium
cards.subtitle: Campbell Hall
cards.notes: Located in the renovated Campbell Hall, this atrium provides a modern space for students living in the STEM learning community to connect and study.
cards.short_summary: A modern atrium in Campbell Hall that supports the building's living-learning community.
cards.evidence_claim: John Burlow Campbell Hall houses the Jones Center Atrium, which serves as a key facility in the building.
cards.source_title: Small Group Venues | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Accessible to residents of Campbell Hall and students using the Jones Center services.

cards.title: The Stairwell Nooks
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Floors 1 & 2
cards.notes: Don't overlook the landings in the front stairwell. These reading nooks offer unique, semi-private seating with views of the campus quad.
cards.short_summary: Quiet reading nooks located on the landings of the library's front stairwell.
cards.evidence_claim: McCain Library features reading nooks in the front stairwell on Floors 1 and 2, including a bay window landing.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the main front stairwell of the library.

cards.title: The Quad Hammocks
cards.subtitle: Main Campus Quad
cards.notes: The heart of campus is more than just a walkway. Students often hang hammocks here to relax between classes or participate in weekly outdoor yoga sessions.
cards.short_summary: The central campus green space used for relaxation, hammocking, and community yoga.
cards.evidence_claim: The Woodruff Quad is used by students for hanging out in hammocks and participating in weekly yoga sessions.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space; hammocks are student-provided or checked out from Campus Rec.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces, cultural events, and recreational activities at Agnes Scott College that require no admission or purchase.

cards.title: Stargazing Open House
cards.subtitle: Monthly Astronomy Events
cards.notes: Attend free monthly open houses featuring lectures, planetarium shows, and telescope viewings. Events are open to the public during the academic year.
cards.short_summary: Free monthly astronomy lectures and telescope viewings at the campus observatory.
cards.evidence_claim: For 70 years, Bradley Observatory has welcomed guests to our open houses monthly during the academic year. The event is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Open House Series - Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Open one Friday evening per month at 7 p.m. or 8 p.m. during the semester.

cards.title: Contemporary Art Viewing
cards.subtitle: Dana Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Explore rotating contemporary art exhibitions in this teaching gallery. Admission is free for students and the general public to view diverse visual works.
cards.short_summary: A free campus art gallery hosting rotating exhibitions and student-focused visual literacy programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dalton Gallery operates as a teaching gallery... Exhibitions engage with on campus conversations. Admission is free.
cards.source_title: The Dalton Gallery: About Dalton Gallery
cards.access_notes: Located in the Dana Fine Arts Building; check gallery website for current exhibition hours.

cards.title: Self-Guided Tree Tour
cards.subtitle: Campus-Wide Nature Walk
cards.notes: Follow a self-guided tour of over 40 historic trees across 100 acres. Use QR codes on plaques to learn about the biology and history of the campus canopy.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided botanical tour featuring historic trees and QR-coded educational plaques.
cards.evidence_claim: The tour, which includes more than 40 historic trees on Agnes Scott's beautiful tree-lined campus, covers topics ranging from history and biology to sustainability.
cards.access_notes: Accessible outdoors across the campus grounds at any time.

cards.title: Historic Library Study
cards.subtitle: Public Access Research Space
cards.notes: Study in a historic architectural setting. The library offers free visitor access and a visitor log for those using the physical collections and quiet spaces.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus library providing free study space and research access for visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: Library privileges extended to alumnae, visitors and other 'guest users' from the general public... Please sign in and out the Visitor Log.
cards.access_notes: Visitor hours: Mon-Thu 10AM-7PM, Fri 10AM-6PM, Sat 10AM-4PM, Sun 4PM-7PM. Restricted during exams.

cards.title: Free Music Concerts
cards.subtitle: Department of Music Events
cards.notes: Enjoy free performances by student ensembles and guest artists. Most concerts are held in Maclean Auditorium or Gaines Chapel and require no tickets.
cards.short_summary: Regularly scheduled free musical performances open to the campus and local community.
cards.evidence_claim: All Music Department concerts and events are free and open to the public unless otherwise noted. No ticket necessary.
cards.source_title: Upcoming Music Events - Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Check the music department calendar for specific event dates and times.

cards.title: Open Lap Swimming
cards.subtitle: Olympic-Sized Pool Access
cards.notes: Students can use the Olympic-sized pool for lap swimming during designated open hours. Access is free with a valid student ID card.
cards.short_summary: Free lap swimming for students at the campus athletic complex pool.
cards.evidence_claim: Open swim hours are available for students who want to stay in shape with lap swimming... offered to Agnes Scott students free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Requires student ID; check the athletics website for current open swim schedules.

cards.title: Student Social Lounges
cards.subtitle: Commuter and Student Spaces
cards.notes: Relax or meet friends in the dedicated student lounges. These spaces provide comfortable seating and a social atmosphere for all Scotties between classes.
cards.short_summary: Central campus hub featuring free social lounges and meeting spaces for students.
cards.evidence_claim: We can make your life a little easier by providing you with lounges specifically for you in the Alston Campus Center.
cards.source_title: Commuter Student Information | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Open daily for student use; specific rooms like 114 offer workout spaces.

cards.title: Free Equipment Checkout
cards.subtitle: Bikes, Hammocks, and Games
cards.notes: Borrow bicycles, hammocks, frisbees, and lawn games for free. The checkout program encourages students to enjoy the campus outdoors without buying gear.
cards.short_summary: A free rental program for students to borrow outdoor recreation and sports equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: We offer a free recreational equipment checkout program to all students. Reserve bicycles, hammocks, Frisbees...
cards.source_title: ASC Campus Recreation - Agnes Scott College Athletics
cards.access_notes: Visit room 213 in the Woodruff Athletics Center to check out equipment with a student ID.

cards.title: Weekly Quad Yoga
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Wellness Classes
cards.notes: Join free weekly yoga sessions held on the main quad. These classes are open to the entire campus community and focus on relaxation and wellness.
cards.short_summary: Free weekly outdoor yoga classes for students and staff on the central campus lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Bring your mat to the main quad where yoga is offered once a week to the entire Agnes Scott community... free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Held once a week; weather permitting. Check Campus Recreation for the current schedule.

cards.title: Scale Model Solar System
cards.subtitle: Interactive Science Plaza
cards.notes: Walk through a scale model of the solar system at this interactive outdoor plaza. It features interpretive signage and demonstrates the relative sizes of planets.
cards.short_summary: An educational outdoor plaza featuring a scale model of the solar system and astronomical markers.
cards.evidence_claim: Outside the observatory is an interactive plaza... It features the Metro-Atlanta Scale Model Solar System (MASS) Project.
cards.source_title: The Bradley Observatory in Decatur holds its FREE open house - Atlanta on the Cheap
cards.access_notes: Open public outdoor space located adjacent to the Bradley Observatory.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the historic McCain Library to modern science lounges, these ten spots offer the best environments for focused academic work at Agnes Scott College.

cards.title: Main Reading Room
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Study by the fireplace in this historic space featuring large windows and comfortable couches. It is a central hub for focused reading.
cards.short_summary: A grand, historic reading room on the first floor of McCain Library featuring a fireplace and large windows.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Reading Room on Floor 1 of McCain Library features couches by the fireplace and study tables.
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; current students can swipe in after 10:30 PM until 1 AM.

cards.title: Elmore Reading Room
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Ground Floor
cards.notes: Enjoy scenic views of the Science Quad from curved couches. This ground-floor space offers a bright, modern atmosphere for group or solo work.
cards.short_summary: A scenic study area on the ground floor of McCain Library overlooking the Science Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kate Durr Elmore Reading Room on the Ground Floor features scenic seating facing the Science Quad and a half-moon couch.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the ground floor entrance; open during library hours.

cards.title: Cameron Reading Terrace
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Take your books outside to the rocking chairs on this terrace. It is a designated area where cell phone calls and fresh air are permitted.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor terrace at McCain Library equipped with rocking chairs and WiFi.
cards.evidence_claim: The Elizabeth Henderson Cameron Reading Terrace features rocking chairs and WiFi, and is a place where cell phone calls are allowed.
cards.source_title: Favorite Study Spots in McCain Library
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access during library hours; located on the first floor.

cards.title: Floor 3 Silent Study
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Floor 3
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for absolute silence. This zone prohibits talking and electronic devices to ensure a distraction-free environment.
cards.short_summary: A strictly silent study floor in McCain Library for distraction-free work.
cards.evidence_claim: Floor 3 and Stack 3 are designated quiet floors where no talking or electronic devices are permitted.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; strictly enforced silence policy.

cards.title: Bullock Graduate Lounge
cards.subtitle: Bullock Science Center
cards.notes: Utilize this dedicated lounge for graduate and post-bacc students. It provides a quiet, centrally located space for advanced research and meetings.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated study and meeting lounge for graduate students in the Bullock Science Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduate and post-bacc students have access to a dedicated lounge space centrally located in the Bullock Science Center.
cards.source_title: Advising & Student Resources | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Restricted to graduate and post-baccalaureate students.

cards.title: Luchsinger Lounge
cards.subtitle: Alston Campus Center
cards.notes: Study by the grand fireplace in the 'Fireplace Lounge.' This cozy spot offers comfortable furniture and views of the campus quad.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable lounge in the Alston Campus Center known for its grand fireplace.
cards.evidence_claim: The Amelia Davis Luchsinger Lounge, dubbed the 'Fireplace Lounge,' features comfortable furniture and is located in the Alston Campus Center.
cards.source_title: Small Group Venues | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Open during Alston Campus Center building hours.

cards.title: Jones Center
cards.subtitle: Campbell Hall
cards.notes: Access peer tutoring and collaborative study areas in this renovated living-learning center. It is designed for intuitive, communal academic work.
cards.short_summary: A learning center in Campbell Hall providing academic support and study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Campbell Hall houses several learning centers, including the Jones Center for Academic Excellence, which features intuitive workspaces.
cards.access_notes: Located in Campbell Hall; accessible to students during building hours.

cards.title: Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: McCain Library, Various Floors
cards.notes: Reserve a private room for 2-8 people via LibCal. These rooms are ideal for collaborative projects and require a key checkout from the desk.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms in McCain Library designed for group collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: McCain Library has five group study rooms that can be reserved for up to two hours per day via the LibCal system.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces and Carrels | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Reservation required; key must be checked out at the first-floor desk.

cards.title: Commuter Lounge
cards.subtitle: Alston Campus Center
cards.notes: Find a home base between classes in this dedicated space for off-campus students. It features lockers and comfortable seating for long study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated lounge and locker area for commuter students in the Alston Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alston Campus Center provides lounges specifically for commuter students, along with lockers for the academic year.
cards.source_title: Commuter Student Information | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Primarily for commuter students; open during building hours.

cards.title: Observatory Library
cards.subtitle: Bradley Observatory
cards.notes: Study in a unique seminar room surrounded by astronomical history. This quiet space is located within the campus's research observatory.
cards.short_summary: A library and seminar room located within the Bradley Observatory building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bradley Observatory building contains a library/seminar room and a student computer lab.
cards.access_notes: Open during observatory building hours; check for seminar schedules.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the walkable corridors and commercial districts surrounding Agnes Scott College, from the historic Decatur Square to the Old Depot District.

cards.title: Decatur Square
cards.subtitle: The Historic Heart of Decatur
cards.notes: Walk three blocks north to reach this central plaza, home to the historic courthouse and frequent community festivals.
cards.short_summary: A central pedestrian plaza and historic district located just north of the Agnes Scott campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Decatur Square is a 15-block walkable district centered around the old DeKalb County courthouse, located a short walk from Agnes Scott.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a public plaza; business hours vary.

cards.title: East College Avenue
cards.subtitle: The Campus Frontage
cards.notes: Stroll along the northern edge of campus to find the Dalton Gallery and historic college-owned rental homes.
cards.short_summary: The primary thoroughfare bordering the northern side of the Agnes Scott College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Agnes Scott College is located at 141 E. College Ave, and the street features college-owned historic homes like Agnes Arbor.
cards.source_title: Agnes Scott College Opens Three Historic Decatur Homes for Short-Term Rental
cards.access_notes: Public street with sidewalk access bordering the campus.

cards.title: South Candler Street
cards.subtitle: Historic Residential Corridor
cards.notes: Visit Charis Books & More, a historic feminist bookstore located at the corner of this residential street.
cards.short_summary: A historic residential street forming the eastern boundary of the college campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Charis Books & More is located at 184 S. Candler Street on the Agnes Scott campus corner.
cards.source_title: Charis Books & More - Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Public street; bookstore open Mon-Sat 10am-7pm, Sun 12pm-6pm.

cards.title: Old Depot District
cards.subtitle: The Railroad Corridor
cards.notes: Explore this district anchored by the 1891 train depot, featuring local eateries and service providers.
cards.short_summary: A commercial district near the railroad tracks that caters to the local neighborhood and students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Old Depot District is a collection of locally owned businesses that cater to the nearby students at Agnes Scott College.
cards.access_notes: Walkable district located just north of the college across the tracks.

cards.title: West Ponce District
cards.subtitle: Dining and Fitness Hub
cards.notes: Walk northwest to find coffee shops like Dancing Goats and various fitness studios along this corridor.
cards.short_summary: A retail and dining district extending along West Ponce de Leon Avenue from the Square.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Ponce district features neighborhood-serving retailers, restaurants like Chai Pani, and fitness studios.
cards.access_notes: Public commercial district with wide sidewalks.

cards.title: Church Street
cards.subtitle: The MARTA Connection
cards.notes: Follow this street south from the Decatur MARTA station to reach the pedestrian tunnel leading to campus.
cards.short_summary: A primary north-south street connecting the downtown MARTA station to the Agnes Scott area.
cards.evidence_claim: Visitors exit the MARTA terminal on the Church Street side and head south to reach the college entrance.
cards.access_notes: Public street providing direct pedestrian access to campus via a tunnel.

cards.title: South McDonough Street
cards.subtitle: Western Campus Boundary
cards.notes: Walk along the western edge of campus to find the Higher Education Hub and access to the Oakhurst neighborhood.
cards.short_summary: A street forming the western boundary of the Agnes Scott campus, connecting to downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The Higher Education Hub is located at 342 S. McDonough Street, adjacent to the college campus.
cards.source_title: Higher Education Hub - Agnes Scott College Calendar
cards.access_notes: Public street bordering the campus and residential areas.

cards.title: Sycamore Street
cards.subtitle: Historic Home Row
cards.notes: Explore some of Decatur's oldest homes and the public library along this quiet, tree-lined street.
cards.short_summary: A historic residential street known for its large 19th-century homes and proximity to the Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Sycamore Street contains some of the largest historic homes in Decatur, including the ca. 1830 High House.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street with sidewalk access.

cards.title: East Trinity Place
cards.subtitle: Downtown Retail Block
cards.notes: Find quick-service dining options like Chick-fil-A and local shops just a few blocks north of campus.
cards.short_summary: A commercial street in downtown Decatur featuring various retail and dining establishments.
cards.evidence_claim: Businesses like Chick-fil-A and Dairy Queen are located along East Trinity Place in the downtown district.
cards.access_notes: Public commercial street with standard business hours.

cards.title: East Court Square
cards.subtitle: The Square's Eastern Edge
cards.notes: Visit the iconic Brick Store Pub or grab coffee at Bellwood Coffee on this bustling downtown block.
cards.short_summary: A high-activity commercial block bordering the eastern side of the Decatur Square.
cards.evidence_claim: East Court Square is home to destination dining like Brick Store Pub and local coffee shops like Bellwood Coffee.
cards.access_notes: Public street bordering the pedestrian plaza of the Square.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique customs of Agnes Scott College, from century-old class rivalries and onyx ring ceremonies to the modern ritual of ringing the bell for career success.

cards.title: Black Cat Week
cards.subtitle: A Century of Class Rivalry
cards.notes: Participate in a week of spirit competitions ending in a bonfire. It began in 1915 as a prank night between first-years and sophomores.
cards.short_summary: Black Cat is a week-long spirit competition and orientation finale that has defined the Agnes Scott experience since 1915.
cards.evidence_claim: Black Cat began in 1915 as a prank night between first-year students and sophomores and now marks the end of orientation.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall, typically concluding orientation for new students.

cards.title: Sophomore Ring Ceremony
cards.subtitle: The Iconic Black Onyx
cards.notes: Receive your class ring, a black onyx stone inscribed with 'ASC'. This rite of passage has united generations of Scotties since 1935.
cards.short_summary: A formal ceremony where sophomores receive their signature black onyx class rings, a tradition dating back to 1935.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sophomore Ring Ceremony is a rite of passage where students receive onyx rings inscribed with 'ASC' and their class year.
cards.source_title: Sophomore Ring Ceremony - Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the sophomore year; family and friends are invited to attend.

cards.title: Ringing the Bell
cards.subtitle: Celebrating Post-Grad Success
cards.notes: Head to the Main Hall tower to ring the bell after landing a job or grad school spot. Sign your name inside the tower for posterity.
cards.short_summary: Seniors ring the historic bell in Main Hall to announce their post-graduation plans, such as job offers or graduate school acceptances.
cards.evidence_claim: Since 1992, seniors ring the bell in Main Tower when they receive a job offer or graduate school acceptance.
cards.source_title: ASC Decoded: Ringing the Bell – Perspective
cards.access_notes: The bell is located in the tower of Main Hall; ringing typically occurs on Friday afternoons in the spring.

cards.title: Senior Investiture
cards.subtitle: The Parade of Leaders
cards.notes: Watch the senior class parade through campus in their academic regalia. This ceremony formally recognizes seniors as campus leaders.
cards.short_summary: An annual fall ceremony and parade that honors the senior class as they begin their final year at the college.
cards.evidence_claim: Senior Investiture began in 1908 and was reimagined in 2021 to include a campus-wide parade and community picnic.
cards.access_notes: Held at the start of the academic year on the Main Quad.

cards.title: Honor Code Signing
cards.subtitle: A Commitment to Integrity
cards.notes: Sign the Honor Pledge during orientation to join a community of trust. This tradition grants students freedoms like self-scheduled exams.
cards.short_summary: New students formally sign the Agnes Scott Honor Pledge, a cornerstone of campus life that dates back to 1906.
cards.evidence_claim: During orientation, each student pledges support to the Honor System and individually signs the Honor Code in Buttrick Hall.
cards.access_notes: The signing ceremony takes place in Buttrick Hall during new student orientation.

cards.title: Pancake Jam
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Finals Fuel
cards.notes: Eat pancakes served by faculty and staff to fuel your late-night study sessions. Enjoy music and dancing before the exam period begins.
cards.short_summary: A late-night breakfast event held every semester before finals where faculty and staff serve pancakes to students.
cards.evidence_claim: Pancake Jam is a twice-yearly event where faculty and staff serve breakfast food to students from 9pm to 10pm before exams.
cards.access_notes: Held in Evans Hall; pancakes are typically served from 9:00 PM to 10:00 PM.

cards.title: AgnesPalooza
cards.subtitle: Spring Semester Celebration
cards.notes: Celebrate the return from spring break with a week of festivals and dance parties. Each year features a unique theme and live events.
cards.short_summary: A week-long spring festival featuring music, dancing, and themed activities to celebrate the second half of the semester.
cards.evidence_claim: AgnesPalooza began in the 1990s and is a week full of events including a festival and dance party held after spring break.
cards.access_notes: An annual spring event; locations vary across campus based on the year's theme.

cards.title: Founder's Day
cards.subtitle: Honoring the College's Roots
cards.notes: Celebrate the college's 1889 founding every February. The event features speakers and performances reflecting on the school's mission.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration in February that commemorates the founding of the college and its history.
cards.evidence_claim: Founder's Day dates back to 1918 and is celebrated every year, usually in February, with speakers and student performances.
cards.source_title: Agnes Scott Traditions | Campus Traditions & Student Life
cards.access_notes: Held annually in February; open to the entire campus community.

cards.title: Rushing the Quad
cards.subtitle: Midnight Spirit Kickoff
cards.notes: Join your classmates at midnight on the Monday of Black Cat week to decorate the Quad in your class color.
cards.short_summary: A midnight ritual where students decorate the central campus quad in their specific class colors to kick off Black Cat week.
cards.evidence_claim: Students begin Black Cat at midnight on Monday with 'Rushing the Quad' to decorate in their class color.
cards.access_notes: Occurs at midnight on the first Monday of Black Cat week on the Main Quad.

cards.title: Junior Jaunt
cards.subtitle: Legacy of Charity and Skits
cards.notes: Learn about this historic fundraiser where classes performed skits and crowned a queen based on money raised for charity.
cards.short_summary: A historic tradition from the 1950s-1980s involving class skits and fundraising for charity.
cards.evidence_claim: Junior Jaunt (1954-1980) was an event where the class that raised the most money for charity had a representative crowned Queen.
cards.access_notes: This is a defunct tradition, now preserved in the college's historical archives.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Agnes Scott College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to the essential traditions, campus hubs, and local spots that define the first few days for new Scotties in Decatur.

cards.title: Sign the Honor Pledge
cards.subtitle: A cornerstone tradition of campus life
cards.notes: Join your class to formally commit to the Honor System, a defining aspect of the Agnes Scott community since 1906.
cards.short_summary: New students sign the Honor Pledge during orientation to uphold standards of honesty and personal integrity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Honor Pledge Ceremony is a key part of New Student Orientation, typically held on the first Friday of the move-in period.
cards.access_notes: Required for all new students during the Legacy orientation program.

cards.title: First Meal at Evans
cards.subtitle: The main campus dining hub
cards.notes: Gather with new friends for all-you-care-to-eat meals featuring international fare and made-to-order stations.
cards.short_summary: Evans Dining Hall is the primary dining location on campus, offering a variety of meal options for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Evans Dining Hall is the central all-you-care-to-eat location on campus for students to catch up with friends.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; weekend hours typically include brunch and dinner services.

cards.title: Explore Alston Center
cards.subtitle: The heart of student activity
cards.notes: Visit the Hub to check out recreational equipment like hammocks or bikes for a relaxing afternoon on the quad.
cards.short_summary: Alston Campus Center houses student organizations, a fitness room, and the campus 'Hub' for equipment rentals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alston Campus Center includes a fitness room and the Hub, where students can check out recreational equipment free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Central campus location; accessible with student ID for specific rooms and equipment.

cards.title: Find a Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Historic architecture and quiet spaces
cards.notes: Scope out your favorite study spot in this historic building, which offers late-night hours on Sundays.
cards.short_summary: McCain Library provides extensive research resources and diverse study environments for Agnes Scott students.
cards.evidence_claim: McCain Library is open until 1 a.m. on Sundays during the academic year for student use.
cards.source_title: Hours and Contact | Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Student ID required for late-night swipe access after 10:30 p.m. on Sundays.

cards.title: Relax on the Quad
cards.subtitle: The central green space
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or a borrowed hammock to the main quad for a classic campus afternoon outdoors.
cards.short_summary: Woodruff Quad is the central outdoor gathering space for events, relaxation, and campus traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Woodruff Quadrangle is a primary site for campus activities, including the 'Rushing the Quad' tradition during Black Cat week.
cards.access_notes: Open public outdoor space on campus.

cards.title: Late Night at Mollie's
cards.subtitle: Casual dining and snacks
cards.notes: Grab a burger or a wrap at this lower-level Alston spot, open late on weekends for a quick bite.
cards.short_summary: Mollie's Grill offers a variety of grilled favorites and convenience items in the Alston Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Mollie's Grill is located in the Alston Campus Center and has weekend hours from 2:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Located in the lower level of Alston; accepts meal swipes and declining balance.

cards.title: Stargaze at Bradley
cards.subtitle: Astronomy and planetarium shows
cards.notes: Check the calendar for monthly Friday open houses to view the stars through the Beck Telescope.
cards.short_summary: Bradley Observatory hosts monthly open houses with lectures and telescope viewings for the community.
cards.evidence_claim: The observatory hosts a free open house every month during the semester on a Friday evening.
cards.source_title: Open House Series - Agnes Scott College
cards.access_notes: Open houses typically start at 7 p.m. or 8 p.m. on select Fridays.

cards.title: Walk to Decatur Square
cards.subtitle: Local shops and dining nearby
cards.notes: Take a short walk north to explore the local boutiques and cafes in the heart of downtown Decatur.
cards.short_summary: Decatur Square is a vibrant district within walking distance of campus, offering numerous student-friendly spots.
cards.evidence_claim: Agnes Scott's campus is a short three-block walk from the Decatur MARTA station and the surrounding square.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via a pedestrian tunnel beneath the railroad tracks from campus.

cards.title: Swim at Woodruff
cards.subtitle: Recreation and fitness facilities
cards.notes: Visit the Olympic-sized pool for open swim hours or use the track for a weekend morning run.
cards.short_summary: The Woodruff Athletic Complex features a pool, gym, and track for student recreation and varsity sports.
cards.evidence_claim: Open swim hours are available for students in the Olympic-sized swimming pool located in the Woodruff Athletic Complex.
cards.access_notes: Student ID required for entry; check seasonal hours for the pool and track.

cards.title: Coffee at Black Cat
cards.subtitle: A student-favorite cafe
cards.notes: Enjoy a specialty coffee or smoothie in this cozy cafe named after the college's oldest tradition.
cards.short_summary: Black Cat Coffee is a campus cafe serving Ebrik Coffee and snacks, located in the Alston Campus Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Black Cat Coffee is located adjacent to Mollie's Grille and serves a full range of coffees and light snacks.
cards.access_notes: Open weekdays and select weekend hours; accepts declining balance dollars.
